text:
maria: quick heads-up 2 the team: i hacked a migration sketch for the prefetch consistency contract. want a sanity check before i turn it into an RFC.

alex: dropping in. TL;DR?

maria: ensure no read-after-write regressions across prefix handoffs and keep eviction fast-path non-disruptive. proposed approach: tiny dual-read-safe markers on prefixes + a soft-drain lease on old owner, plus an async reconciler to repair any drift.

kai: explain marker shape + cost. are we adding a read-path hit for every request?

maria: marker = 1-byte state + epoch + owner-id (encoded in prefix metadata). runtime only consults marker on misses or on detected lease-change; normal hits skip it. so steady-state cost = minimal.

jordan: if a hot prefix flips owners a lot, won't markers + reconciler cause churn?

maria: mitigations: (1) markers auto-expire with TTL tied to lease window, (2) reconciler runs probabilistically based on flip frequency, (3) cap repair attempts per-tenant and backoff.

alex: concrete handoff flow?

maria: flow:
```
1) candidate asks leader to take prefix -> leader writes soft-lease to metastore (epoch X)
2) old owner sets marker(prefix, owner=old, epoch=X, drain=true)
3) old owner stops accepting mutations for that prefix but continues serving reads until safe
4) new owner performs dual-read: read from local cache -> if miss or marker indicates different owner, proxy/check old owner for latest value
5) once inflight writes drained and residency low, old owner clears marker and releases lease
6) async reconciler sweeps stale markers and repairs missing k/v if necessary
```

kai: split-brain risk if leader crashes mid-handoff?

maria: mitigate via CAS-based lease tokens in metastore and marker epochs. new leader sees mismatched epochs and either extends or aborts handoff; marker includes owner-id+epoch so detection is deterministic.

jordan: ops-bot, what telemetry should we emit to monitor this safely?

ops-bot: deploy-bot: recommended metrics -> ["prefix_handoff_started", "prefix_handoff_failed", "dual_read_proxy_count", "marker_created", "marker_expired", "marker_swept", "handoff_latency_ms", "hot_flip_rate_per_prefix"]. Suggested alerts on handoff_failed spikes and hot_flip_rate exceeding sane threshold. :bell:

alex: next steps: maria -> RFC with failure-mode matrix and test plan; kai -> prototype marker field in in-memory header with unit test; jordan -> ops playbook for reconciler (timeouts, kill-switch); i'll run perf microbench on dual-read path.

maria: will draft RFC by EOD with regression tests + chaos plan. :thumbsup:

kai: one more ask: preserve client-visible linearizability for writes. if we can't, we need an explicit compatibility policy.

maria: agreed. RFC will include litmus tests for R/W linearizability and rollout gating.

alex: cool. no blockers from me. ping runtime when RFC ready and we'll schedule design review.
